To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the local structure of ATLS of different stoichiometry is similar and that the oxide-ion migration is not only channel/ interstitial but also tetrahedral oxygen atoms are involved.

the local structure of apatite-type La 9.33− x Fe x Si 6− y O 26.33− z (H 2 O) 0.33 ( x = 1, 2, 3; y = 0, 1, 4; z = 0, ± 1) solid solutions can be characterized by the formation of Si–O–Si bridges and that this structural feature is related to the oxide-ion migration.

(i) the local structure of ATLS can be characterized by IR spectroscopy; (ii) the presence of [SiO4] group interactions can be indirectly confirmed in the systems; (iii) the presence of Al and Fe in ATLS can lead to a decrease in oxide-ion conductivity; (iv) in the systems studied the transport properties are governed by oxide-ion diffusion in the channels and/or interstitial sites.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure, transport properties and oxygen isotope tracer diffusion in the systems of La(Fe,Al)O 2.5+x (x = 0.0, 0.1, 0.15, 0.2) and La 2 (Fe,Al) 3 O 8+x (x = −0.2, 0.0).

the synthesis and characterization of a new family of apatite-type silicates with the general formula Ln 1-x M x Si 2 O 5 (M=Al,Fe) and Ln 1-x-y M x M y Si 2 O (M=Fe,Al) with the aim to understand the role of the dopant cations on the structure and the properties of the apatite-type materials.
the structure and properties of apatite-type La 1-x-y A y Fe x Si 1-x-y O 2+δ (A = Ca, Sr, Ba) solid solutions with different cation stoichiometry.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
both Fe and Al dopants can affect both the structure and transport properties of ATLS.
both the structure and properties of ATLS depend strongly on their stoichiometry.

the presence of cations in the apatitic structure, in particular Fe 3+, is responsible for the increase of the conductivity of La 9.33-x-y Si 6 O 26-x F x (Fe 2+ ) y O 2-δ, while the increase of Al 3+ content in the apatites leads to a decrease of their conductivity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the structure of ATLS is more complex than previously assumed and the oxide-ion transport in this system is not only due to the migration of channel oxygen atoms but is also due to the migration in the tetrahedrons.
the oxide-ion migration in ATLS is a cooperative process, involving both channel/interstitial and tetrahedron atoms, and the migration mechanism depends on the local structure.
the oxide-ion conductivity of ATLS is determined by the presence of the cation vacancies and the [SiO 2 ] group interaction in the lattice.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the local structure and the transport properties of ATLS can be tuned by varying the composition.

the local structure is not the only factor that determines the oxide-ion migration in ATLS and the presence of cations with different valences and sizes in the apatites can significantly influence the transport properties.
the presence of cations in the apatites, which are not directly involved in the oxide ion conduction mechanism, can significantly influence the transport properties of the system.
